data.name: Nethergate: Resurrection
data.detailed_description:
Spiderweb Software's classic adventure of treachery and battle in ancient times has returned! Travel back to ancient Britannia for a tale of cunning foes, vicious battles, and a race to rediscover the lost secrets of magic.

Britannia is a land ravaged by war. The natives of this land, the savage Celts, have long been subjugated by the Roman invaders. At last, they have risen up in bloody rebellion. Battles rage across the land. Cities are sacked, the inhabitants massacred. And, lost in the chaos, in the small, forgotten valley of Shadowvale, a plan is being formed.

Soon, a band of barbarians will rediscover the lost secrets of magic. They will find a way to rid their lands of their oppressors forever. And you, as the Celtic warriors, will attempt to free your people.

Or you, as the Romans, will attempt to crush them. For the good of the Empire.

Key Features

  • Two different sides, the powerful Romans and the savage and cunning Celts. Each side has a completely different full-length adventure.
  • Enormous game world, with dozens of dungeons and many characters and quests.
  • Fascinating storyline. Fight for freedom, or further the glory of the Empire.
  • Lost secrets of magic! Dozens of spells and hundreds of hidden magical artifacts.
  • Innovative story and unique setting. Unlike any fantasy game you've ever played.

reviews.review:
Nethergate: Resurrection is one of those role-playing games that feels like a relic from a different age, not just because of its graphics, but because of the way it approaches storytelling and player engagement. Developed and published by Spiderweb Software, the game revisits the studio's original Nethergate with a larger scope, enhanced content, and numerous quality-of-life improvements. Set in a mythical interpretation of Roman-occupied Britain, it presents a conflict between the expanding Roman Empire and the native Celts, weaving historical elements together with folklore, magic, and ancient mysteries. The result is a role-playing experience that stands apart from the crowded fantasy genre by embracing a setting rarely explored in games.

What immediately distinguishes Nethergate: Resurrection is its two-sided campaign design. Players can either command a group of Roman soldiers carrying out the Empire's will or lead a band of Celts fighting to preserve their traditions and homeland. These campaigns are more than alternate perspectives; they feature different quests, encounters, abilities, and narrative developments. Playing both stories provides a broader understanding of the world and its inhabitants, making the conflict feel layered and believable. Spiderweb Software deserves credit for presenting a war where both sides possess understandable motivations, allowing players to appreciate the complexities of conquest, resistance, and cultural identity.

Exploration plays a major role throughout the adventure. The game world is filled with hidden locations, magical treasures, optional storylines, and dangerous dungeons waiting to be uncovered. Shadowy forests, Roman encampments, forgotten ruins, and mystical realms contribute to an atmosphere that constantly encourages curiosity. The Resurrection edition expands significantly on the original release with additional areas, new quests, and more powerful artifacts to discover. Despite its age, the sense of reward for thorough exploration remains highly satisfying, especially for players who enjoy uncovering secrets through patience rather than objective markers and constant guidance.

Combat embraces a traditional turn-based system that prioritizes planning over speed. Each encounter requires players to consider positioning, equipment, and the strengths of their party members. Romans tend to rely on superior military discipline and equipment, while Celtic characters have greater access to mystical powers and unconventional tactics. This distinction helps ensure that each campaign feels mechanically unique. Battles are not visually impressive by modern standards, but they remain engaging because they are built around strategic decisions instead of flashy effects. Fans of classic computer RPGs will likely appreciate the deliberate pacing, while newcomers may need time to adjust to its slower and more methodical approach.

The writing is another area where Nethergate: Resurrection excels. Spiderweb Software has always relied heavily on narrative to compensate for modest production values, and that philosophy is on full display here. Conversations with non-player characters often reveal details about the world's politics, myths, and history, helping establish a strong sense of place. Celtic legends and supernatural beings are woven naturally into the setting, creating a world that feels mysterious without becoming overly fantastical. There is an undeniable charm to the game's emphasis on text and imagination, reminding players that compelling stories do not necessarily require expensive cinematics or voice acting.

Of course, the game is not without its shortcomings. Its interface is functional but dated, and the visual presentation reflects its independent origins. Character sprites, environmental details, and animations lack the refinement found in contemporary role-playing games. Some players may also find the extensive reading and occasional backtracking cumbersome. Nethergate: Resurrection demands patience and a willingness to embrace older design conventions, which means it will not appeal to everyone. However, for players who enjoy classic CRPGs, these limitations are easier to forgive when weighed against the game's depth and ambition.

In the end, Nethergate: Resurrection remains an excellent example of old-school role-playing done with passion and creativity. Its uncommon setting, meaningful dual campaigns, extensive exploration, and tactical combat combine to create an experience that continues to hold up for dedicated genre fans. While it may never win over players seeking modern production values, it succeeds remarkably well at delivering a thoughtful and immersive adventure rooted in history and myth. It is a title that demonstrates how strong writing and intelligent game design can leave a lasting impression long after technological advancements have moved on.

Rating: 8/10
